headline: Sterling is near 1.3375 dollars, close to its one month high, after UK business surveys for October beat forecasts. Markets price at least three Bank of England rises by April 2027 and expect the Fed to hold next week, while oil near $113.7 (about £85.00) on Gulf tension is a counterweight, with the US surveys due this afternoon.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: The Fed's range is 3.75% to 4% after its September rise. On Friday 23 October Trading Economics put the chance of a hold at the meeting ending on 28 October at about 91%, and the chance of a rise in December at about 80%; Reuters reported on 22 October that oil driven inflation keeps a December rise in view. The Fed is in its quiet period before the decision.

drivers.title: US bond yields and the dollar
drivers.text: The US ten year yield fell by more than 10 basis points to below 5% on Thursday 22 October, a one month low, and was about 4.97% on Friday morning, Trading Economics reported. The dollar index was near 101.6, close to a three week low. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent was near $113.7 (about £84.90) a barrel on Friday 23 October, up about 0.5% in Asian trading and close to its four year high of $114.44 (about £85.40) from 4 May, Trading Economics reported. Iran said seven tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, the New York Times reported US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes after the 3 November midterms, and President Trump said the US was not negotiating with Iran. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75% and money markets price at least three quarter point rises by April 2027, the first possibly on 5 November, after September inflation of 3.5% against 3.4% expected, Trading Economics reported. Sterling held near a one month high on Thursday as money moved into UK bonds. The Chancellor, John Healey, presents the Budget on Wednesday 28 October after public borrowing came in above forecast on 21 October; higher expected UK rates support the pound, while worry about borrowing or tax rises can weigh on it.

drivers.title: Europe and the wider mood
drivers.text: The euro has held just above $1.12 (about £0.84) after a month of losses on unrest in France and its budget problems, and the European Central Bank meets on 29 October, expected to hold at 2.5%. Technology shares sold off on Thursday after results from Meta and Tesla. A weaker euro or a nervous mood in markets tends to steady the dollar.

lower: Further attacks on Gulf shipping or Saudi oil sites pushing Brent above its May high of $114.44 (about £85.40), which would tend to lift the dollar.
Firmer US business surveys this afternoon, which would add to the case for a December Fed rise and lift the dollar.
A Fed statement on 28 October that leans towards a December rise, which would lift US yields and the dollar.
A Budget on 28 October that unsettles the gilt market with more borrowing than expected, which would weigh on the pound.
higher: Stronger UK business surveys, out this morning above forecast, which add to the case for a Bank of England rise on 5 November and support the pound.
Softer US business surveys this afternoon, which would make a December Fed rise less likely and weaken the dollar.
Any sign of talks between the US and Iran, which would bring oil down, ease US inflation worries and weaken the dollar.
A Budget that reassures the gilt market, which would remove a weight on the pound.
watch: The US business surveys come out at 17:45 Dubai today (manufacturing forecast 55.4, services 57.9). Softer US figures would help someone selling pounds for dirhams; firmer ones would weigh on the pound against the dollar.

feed.title: UK business surveys have beaten forecasts
feed.text: The flash October surveys showed UK services at 53.1 against 51.8 expected and manufacturing at 52.8 against about 51.8, both up on September. Firmer UK activity supports the case for a Bank of England rise on 5 November, and the pound gained on the euro, while GBP/USD rose from 1.3380 to 1.3385 within a minute, then slipped to 1.3374 by 08:36 UTC as the dollar firmed across the board, a move no source has yet explained.

feed.title: UK shoppers spent less than expected in September
feed.text: Retail sales volumes fell 0.4% in September against a forecast fall of 0.1%, and fell 0.7% without fuel, though August was revised up to a 0.7% rise; the ONS put the drop down to warm weather hitting winter clothing and a dip in supermarket sales. Weaker spending trims slightly the case for a Bank of England rise on 5 November, which tends to weigh on the pound. The reaction was small: GBP/USD slipped from 1.3388 just before 10:00 Dubai to 1.3384 within a minute, held near 1.3386 for twenty minutes, then recovered to 1.3392.

feed.title: Sterling has eased slightly overnight as the dollar steadied
feed.text: GBP/USD drifted from 1.3401 at 05:35 Dubai to 1.3392 by 06:00 Dubai and was near 1.3394 at 07:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by the same 0.07%, from 1.1220 to 1.1211, so this was the dollar firming rather than the pound weakening. No report explains the move; it came in quiet Asian trading with Brent steady near $113.7 (about £84.90) and the US ten year yield still below 5% at about 4.97%.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as US bond yields fell sharply
feed.text: US government bond yields had their biggest one day fall in more than two years as investors left technology shares for bonds after disappointing results from Meta and Tesla: the ten year yield was down 11 basis points to 5.02% by 19:13 Dubai and below 5% by 20:55 Dubai, Yahoo Finance reported. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, so more dirhams per pound; EUR/USD rose by a similar margin while the pound hardly moved against the euro, so this was the dollar softening. GBP/USD rose from 1.3369 at 19:25 Dubai to 1.3407 by 21:15 Dubai and was near 1.3403 at 22:35 Dubai.

feed.title: Fewer Americans claimed jobless benefits last week
feed.text: New claims for unemployment benefits fell to 194,000 in the week to 17 October, against 200,000 expected, and the week before was revised up to 200,000. Fewer claims point to a US job market that is still firm, which supports the dollar, but the effect was small: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3373 to 1.3368 within a minute of the release, then recovered to about 1.3372 by 12:32 UTC.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed on reports of planned strikes on Iran
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3382 at 14:54 Dubai to 1.3361 by 15:09 Dubai and was near 1.3366 at 15:36 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar margin and the pound hardly moved against the euro, so this was the dollar strengthening. No report ties a piece of news to that quarter hour, but just before it CNBC reported a New York Times account that the US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for a short but intensive operation against Iran after next month's midterm elections, with Brent near $112 (about £84). Gulf tension and dearer oil tend to lift the dollar, so fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as the dollar firmed in a nervous market
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3407 at 13:42 Dubai to 1.3379 by 14:09 Dubai and was near 1.3382 at 14:36 Dubai. EUR/USD fell by about 0.12% over the same half hour while the pound eased only slightly against the euro, so this was mostly the dollar strengthening. No report ties a piece of news to that half hour, but the mood is nervous: Iranian state television said seven tankers were damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz, Brent rose about 3% to near $112 (about £84), European shares fell by around 1%, and a nervous market with dearer oil tends to lift the dollar, so fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped again around midday
feed.text: GBP/USD fell to 1.3397 at 12:08 Dubai, then climbed to 1.3418 by 12:26 Dubai before settling near 1.3408 at 12:38 Dubai. EUR/USD rose from 1.1229 to 1.1242 over the same quarter hour while the euro hardly moved against the pound, so this was the dollar softening rather than the pound rising. No report found explains the move: Trading Economics describes the dollar index as steady near 101.7 on Thursday, with a Fed hold expected next week, and oil has risen rather than fallen this morning.

feed.title: Oil has climbed after a drone strike on a Saudi oil field
feed.text: Brent rose about 1.7% to near $110.70 (about £82.60) a barrel on Thursday morning, Trading Economics reported, after debris from a drone shot down near Aramco's Shaybah field killed two workers and the US ordered non-emergency embassy staff out of Saudi Arabia. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, yet sterling held its ground overnight: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3400 at 22:00 Dubai on Wednesday to 1.3381 by 23:00 Dubai, recovered to about 1.3394, and was near 1.3383 at 06:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased in early trade this morning
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3390 at 06:45 Dubai to 1.3406 by 07:15 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose by a similar margin and the euro barely moved against the pound, so this was the dollar softening rather than the pound rising. No report found explains the move; Reuters described the dollar's recent slide as pausing in Asian trade, with traders waiting for next week's Fed, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan meetings. A softer dollar means more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the dollar softened this evening
feed.text: GBP/USD climbed from 1.3383 at 20:12 Dubai to 1.3394 by 20:30 Dubai, touched 1.3401 at 20:39 Dubai and was near 1.3398 at 21:30 Dubai. The euro gained against the dollar by a similar margin over the same hour, so this was the dollar softening rather than the pound rising. No report found explains the move: the US oil stocks figures came out two hours earlier, and Trading Economics still describes the dollar index as near 101.7, close to its three week low, with the Fed expected to hold next week.

feed.title: Sterling held steady through Governor Bailey's talk
feed.text: Governor Bailey took part in a fireside chat in London on central bank independence, listed by the Bank of England for 14:00 London time. No reported remarks on the 5 November decision had appeared by 13:40 UTC, so no source yet explains any move. GBP/USD was 1.3396 at the start, dipped to 1.3392 within two minutes and was still near 1.3393 a quarter of an hour later, before easing to about 1.3384 by 13:36 UTC.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed to a one month high as rate rise bets firm
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3372 at 11:35 Dubai to 1.3393 by 12:00 Dubai and held near 1.3392 at 12:38 Dubai, while EUR/USD barely moved and the euro fell from 0.8391 to 0.8381 pounds, so this was the pound gaining rather than the dollar weakening. No report ties the climb to fresh news at that time; Trading Economics and BigGo say traders now treat a Bank of England rise to 4% on 5 November as all but certain after this morning's 3.5% inflation figure, with many also expecting a further rise in December. Firmer expectations for UK rates tend to lift the pound, which means more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: UK inflation has come in a little above forecast
feed.text: Prices rose 3.5% in the year to September against 3.4% expected and 3.1% in August, with core inflation up to 2.8% from 2.6% and motor fuel 29.8% dearer than a year earlier, the ONS figures showed. Higher inflation makes the Bank of England rise expected on 5 November more likely, which tends to lift the pound. GBP/USD jumped from 1.3373 to 1.3384 within the minute of the release but gave it back at once and was near 1.3369 at 10:15 Dubai, which suggests the rise was already in the price.

feed.title: The government has approved the Jackdaw gas field
feed.text: The government has cleared Shell's Jackdaw gas field, about 150 miles east of Aberdeen, while a decision on the larger Rosebank oil field is still to come, STV and HuffPost reported. At its peak Jackdaw would supply about 6.5% of UK North Sea gas production, which is too small and too far off to move the pound, and no reaction shows in GBP/USD.

feed.title: A Bank of England policymaker has made the case for higher rates
feed.text: Megan Greene told the London School of Economics on Tuesday evening that the risk of the energy shock feeding into wider inflation is greater than the Bank expected, and that it should lean against that risk early, Reuters reported. Talk of a firmer Bank of England supports the expected rise to 4% on 5 November, which tends to lift the pound. GBP/USD edged up from 1.3370 at 21:00 Dubai to 1.3381 by 21:50 Dubai, a small move that no report ties directly to the speech.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight ahead of UK inflation
feed.text: GBP/USD was 1.3374 at 07:40 Dubai, where it stood at 19:40 Dubai yesterday, after a quiet night between about 1.3370 and 1.3385. Reuters reported from Tokyo that the dollar index was steady at 101.78 after falling 0.2% on Tuesday to a three week low, as lower US Treasury yields and a dip in oil made the dollar less attractive. Brent settled 0.7% lower at $108.79 (about £81) a barrel on Tuesday after touching a five month high, as traders weighed conflicting reports on US and Iran talks.

feed.title: Sterling has given back some of its gains as the dollar firms
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3401 at 18:41 Dubai to 1.3381 by 18:51 Dubai and was near 1.3373 at 19:38 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1250 to 1.1231, so this was mainly a firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. The afternoon rise had come on an unconfirmed report that Qatar and Pakistan had put forward a compromise to revive US and Iran talks, and Bloomberg later quoted a diplomat involved in the talks disputing that a deal was close, though no source gives the time of that comment, so it cannot be tied to this move with confidence. Less hope of a deal tends to support oil and the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped further as US bond yields fall
feed.text: The US ten-year yield fell about five basis points to 5.09% in New York trading, Bloomberg reported, and the dollar fell against every other major currency, with the dollar index down 0.23% at about 101.76, FXStreet reported; neither names a single piece of news behind it, and no US figures were due today. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, so more dirhams per pound. The euro rose by a similar share, so this was a dollar move: GBP/USD climbed from about 1.3370 at 17:00 Dubai to a high near 1.3407 at 18:25 Dubai, most of it in ten minutes from 18:15, then settled near 1.3399.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed this afternoon with no news to explain it
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3349 at 16:11 Dubai to 1.3375 by 16:26 Dubai and was near 1.3371 at 16:38 Dubai, a 0.20% climb in a quarter of an hour. Both sides moved: the euro gained about 0.08% against the dollar while the pound gained about 0.1% against the euro, so a slightly softer dollar and a firmer pound together. No report names a cause for this move; Reuters had described the dollar index at midday as 0.1% lower at 101.85 and the pound as up 0.3% after this morning's jobs figures, with Bank of England rise bets supporting it.

feed.title: Sterling has risen on stronger UK jobs figures
feed.text: Unemployment fell to 4.7% in the three months to August against 4.9% expected, and regular pay growth was 3.7% against 3.6% expected, though total pay including bonuses slowed to 3.7% against a 3.8% forecast, the ONS figures showed. A firmer job market and steady pay make the Bank of England rise expected on 5 November more likely, which lifts the pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3332 to 1.3345 within the minute of the release while EUR/USD did not move, climbed to about 1.3361 by 10:30 Dubai, and held near 1.3349 at 13:10 Dubai even as the euro slipped against the dollar.

feed.title: The dollar has eased overnight, lifting sterling a little
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3308 at midnight Dubai to 1.3332 by 07:30 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from 1.1211 to 1.1227, so this was mainly a softer dollar rather than news about the pound. Reuters reported from Tokyo early on Tuesday that the dollar index had dipped 0.05% to 101.92 and the euro had recovered a little of Monday's 0.25% fall caused by the unrest in France, while Asian shares fell sharply ahead of results from AI companies. Brent rose 0.21% to $109.78 (about £82) a barrel, which would usually support the dollar, so oil was not the cause.

feed.title: A brief spike at 07:02 Dubai was a single large trade
feed.text: GBP/USD on Kraken jumped from 1.3330 to 1.3358 within the minute to 07:02 Dubai and was back at 1.3331 the next minute. EUR/USD did not move and no news report names a cause, so this looks like one large order meeting a thin early morning market rather than a change in the rate.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed as US bond yields climbed this afternoon
feed.text: The US ten-year yield rose about 4.6 basis points to 5.127% by 19:30 Dubai, reversing a fall in the morning, as yields rose worldwide on the unrest in France, FXStreet reported, and the dollar index gained 0.13% to 101.91. Higher US yields draw money into the dollar, so fewer dirhams per pound. The euro fell by a similar share while the pound held steady against the euro, so this was a dollar move: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3335 at 15:00 Dubai to 1.3311 by 20:38 Dubai.
